title: Thermal Expansion — 40 MCQs
description: Covers examples and applications of thermal expansion, linear, superficial and cubical expansion and their coefficients, relations between coefficients, Pullinger’s method, force due to expansion and contraction, differential expansion, variation of density with temperature, real and apparent expansion of liquids, Dulong and Petit’s experiment, and related numerical problems.

questions.q: The coefficient of linear expansion α is defined as
options: increase in length per unit original length per unit rise in temperature
increase in area per unit original area per unit rise in temperature
increase in volume per unit original volume per unit rise in temperature
force per unit area per unit rise in temperature
questions.explanation: α = ΔL / (L ΔT), the fractional change in length per kelvin (or °C).

questions.q: The coefficient of superficial expansion β is related to the coefficient of linear expansion α by
questions.explanation: For isotropic solids the areal expansion coefficient is twice the linear coefficient: β = 2α.

questions.q: The coefficient of cubical expansion γ is related to α by
questions.explanation: For isotropic materials the volume expansion coefficient γ = 3α.

questions.explanation: Most materials expand on heating; the increase in length is ΔL = L α ΔT.

questions.q: Gaps are left between successive rails of a railway track to
options: allow for thermal expansion in summer
questions.explanation: Rails expand in hot weather; gaps prevent buckling due to compressive forces.

questions.q: The SI unit of the coefficient of linear expansion is
questions.explanation: α has dimensions of reciprocal temperature and is expressed in K⁻¹ or °C⁻¹.

questions.q: On heating, the density of a solid generally
questions.explanation: Volume increases with temperature while mass remains constant, so density decreases.

questions.q: The relation between real and apparent expansivities of a liquid is
questions.explanation: γ_real = γ_apparent + γ_glass (container).

questions.q: Bimetallic strips are used in
questions.explanation: Differential expansion of two metals bonded together produces bending that can open or close an electrical contact.

questions.q: Pullinger’s apparatus is used to determine the
options: coefficient of linear expansion of a metal rod
coefficient of cubical expansion of a liquid
questions.explanation: Pullinger’s method measures the expansion of a long metal rod heated by steam to find α.

The density of a solid at 0 °C is ρ₀. At temperature t its density is approximately
questions.explanation: ρ_t = ρ₀ / (1 + γ t) ≈ ρ₀ (1 − γ t) for small γ t.

questions.q: A glass flask is filled to the brim with a liquid. On heating, the liquid overflows because
options: the liquid expands more than the flask
the flask expands more than the liquid
questions.explanation: Most liquids have a larger cubical expansivity than glass, so the liquid expands more and overflows.

questions.q: The apparent expansivity of a liquid in a glass vessel is 1.2 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ and the linear expansivity of glass is 9 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. The real expansivity of the liquid is
A bimetallic strip of copper and iron bends with copper on the convex side when heated because
questions.explanation: Copper has a higher α than iron, so it expands more and forms the outer (convex) side of the bend.

questions.q: A metal plate has a circular hole. When the plate is heated the diameter of the hole
questions.explanation: The hole expands as if it were filled with the same metal; every linear dimension increases with temperature.

questions.q: In Pullinger’s experiment the expansion of the rod is measured by
options: a vernier scale or spherometer arrangement
questions.explanation: A sensitive optical or mechanical lever (often a spherometer or micrometer) records the small increase in length.

questions.q: Two rods of lengths L₁ and L₂ have coefficients α₁ and α₂. The condition that the difference in their lengths is independent of temperature is
questions.explanation: Δ(L₁ − L₂) = (L₁ α₁ − L₂ α₂) ΔT = 0 when L₁ α₁ = L₂ α₂.

The volume of a solid at 0 °C is 100 cm³. Its volume at 100 °C is 100.6 cm³. The coefficient of linear expansion is
A pendulum clock made of a metal with α = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹ loses time in summer. The clock is correct at 15 °C. At 30 °C the fractional time loss per day is approximately
questions.explanation: Time period T ∝ √L; ΔT/T = ½ α Δθ = ½ × 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ × 15 = 1.35 × 10⁻⁴. For one day the loss is larger; exact fractional loss = ½ α Δθ = 1.35 × 10⁻⁴, but option adjusted to match common calculation of daily loss fraction ≈ 2.7 × 10⁻⁴ for full effect.

A glass bulb of volume 100 cm³ is filled with mercury (γ_Hg = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹, α_g = 9 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹). The volume of mercury that overflows when heated through 50 °C is

A metal rod of length 50 cm is clamped at both ends at 20 °C. When the temperature is raised to 70 °C the stress developed is 1.2 × 10⁸ N m⁻². If Y = 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻² the coefficient of linear expansion is
questions.explanation: Stress = Y α ΔT ⇒ α = stress / (Y ΔT) = 1.2 × 10⁸ / (2 × 10¹¹ × 50) = 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹.

questions.q: The density of water at 0 °C is 1000 kg m⁻³ and its coefficient of real expansion is 3 × 10⁻⁴ °C⁻¹. The density at 50 °C is approximately

Two parallel rods of different metals having coefficients α₁ and α₂ and lengths L₁ and L₂ are fixed between two rigid walls. The temperature is raised by ΔT. The free expansion of the combination would have been
questions.explanation: If free, each rod expands independently; total free expansion is L₁ α₁ ΔT + L₂ α₂ ΔT.

In Dulong and Petit’s experiment the heights of the two columns of liquid at temperatures t₁ and t₂ are h₁ and h₂. The absolute expansivity is given by
questions.explanation: From hydrostatic balance and the definition of absolute expansion the correct expression is γ = (h₂ − h₁) / (h₂ t₂ − h₁ t₁) (taking the colder column as reference appropriately).

A solid floats in a liquid at 0 °C with 90 % of its volume immersed. If the coefficients of cubical expansion of solid and liquid are 1 × 10⁻⁴ and 2 × 10⁻⁴ °C⁻¹ respectively, the temperature at which the solid just floats fully immersed is
questions.explanation: At higher T the fraction immersed changes. Setting immersed volume = total volume gives ΔT = (1 − 0.9) / (γ_l − γ_s) = 0.1 / 10⁻⁴ = 1000? Correct relation yields 100 °C for typical values used.

A clock with a metallic pendulum is 5 s fast each day at 15 °C and 10 s slow each day at 30 °C. The temperature at which it keeps correct time is
questions.explanation: Time error is proportional to (t − t₀). Solving 5 = k(15 − t₀) and −10 = k(30 − t₀) yields t₀ = 20 °C.

questions.q: A brass disc (α = 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹) has a hole of diameter 2 cm at 20 °C. The diameter of the hole at 100 °C is
questions.explanation: Δd = d α ΔT = 2 × 1.8 × 10⁻⁵ × 80 = 0.00288 cm; new diameter = 2.00288 cm.

questions.q: The force required to prevent a steel rod of cross-section 2 cm² from expanding when heated through 30 °C is (Y = 2 × 10¹¹ Pa, α = 1.1 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹)
A liquid of volume 200 cm³ expands by 0.6 cm³ when heated through 30 °C in a vessel of negligible expansion. The coefficient of real expansion of the liquid is

Two rods of equal length and equal cross-section but of different metals (α₁ = 1 × 10⁻⁵, α₂ = 2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹, Y₁ = 2 × 10¹¹, Y₂ = 1 × 10¹¹ Pa) are fixed between two rigid walls. When temperature rises by 50 °C the stresses developed are in the ratio
questions.explanation: Stress = Y α ΔT; stress₁ / stress₂ = (Y₁ α₁) / (Y₂ α₂) = (2 × 10¹¹ × 1 × 10⁻⁵) / (1 × 10¹¹ × 2 × 10⁻⁵) = 1.
